policy: Separate equivalence-review queue; these labels are not assigned in groups 001-184. Preserve qualifiers and decide from evidence.

entries.note: Both refer to African metal scenes and share Skinflint/Wrust/Overthrust, but the source includes a wider contemporary mix including Duma and Ohgod. The repository describes a particular NWOBHM/thrash-rooted heavy-metal sound, so full scope equivalence remains unresolved.
Album rock is a format/style category narrower than the generic Rock record, which mentions the album context.

Industrial ambient and dark ambient overlap historically, but the source preserves both named categories and the repository is specifically the menacing dark-ambient idiom. Do not treat all industrial ambient as that narrower form.
Protest-song subset is narrower than the American folk revival movement.
Art song is broader than these individual regional song traditions; their definitions do not establish a generic art-song record.
Aussie pub rock is one Australian rock scene and cannot replace the broader national Australian rock category.
Austropop is specifically German-language Austrian pop practice; source separately lists Austrian pop and austropop.
Rock in Opposition overlaps experimental avant-rock but is a specific movement; the generic avant-rock label remains unresolved.
Dinner jazz is a particular acoustic dining-room practice; background jazz may cover a broader functional category.

Bagpipe is a repertoire/instrument category broader than individual Highland, Irish, Iberian and other regional piping traditions.
Balafon Music (Mande and Voltaic) is a geographically scoped balafon tradition; check the EveryNoise instrumental category before equating the broader label.
Balalaika orchestra is an ensemble tradition; a general balalaika category may include solo/chamber repertoire as well.
Black gospel choir is broader than Baptist gospel in denomination and cannot certify denomination-specific representation.
Repo explicitly scopes performance to period instruments. Source baroque may include modern-instrument performances and broader artist classification.
Bass music is an umbrella over several electronic/bass styles; these narrower dubstep, wave and regional bass records do not establish it as an entry.

Modern electronic bhangra and Punjabi harvest bhangra are explicitly differentiated; retain the broad bhangra label pending scoped alias review. Two separate folk/modern records exist. The source broad bhangra label needs scope review rather than automatic collapse into one branch.
Blues rock is a parent/influence of southern rock, hard rock and related records; those are distinct styles rather than an explicit blues-rock entry.
Balkan brass is a regional tradition within the broader brass-ensemble repertoire/ensemble category.

The repo represents Brazilian samba/bossa-fused drum-and-bass. Every Noise separately lists sambass and brazilian dnb, and the latter’s example is L-Side, so the broad national DnB category is not established as the same subtype.
Samba-jazz is a specific Brazilian jazz hybrid, not the whole national jazz category.
BRock is explicitly the 1980s Brazilian rock wave and Jovem Guarda an earlier specific movement; neither covers Brazilian rock as a generic national scene entry.
Cabaret is a performance/repertoire category spanning these records, not an alias for chanson, standards, torch song or industrial.
Makossa is one Cameroonian popular genre, not the complete Cameroonian pop category.
Galician kantautor is one regional singer-songwriter tradition, while cantautor is a broader Spanish-language artist/category label.
Carnatic is the broad South Indian classical tradition; vocal, instrumental, concert and individual form records remain narrower entries.
